title: Knowledge check: Secure XML Parser Configuration

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly covered in “Secure XML Parser Configuration”?
options: Disabling external entity resolution when unnecessary
questions.answer_key: Disabling external entity resolution when unnecessary
questions.explanation: The attached XML curriculum lists “Disabling external entity resolution when unnecessary” under lesson 144, “Secure XML Parser Configuration”. The other options are from different topics or unrelated areas.

questions.prompt: Which statement is the most reliable rule to remember when applying “Secure XML Parser Configuration”?
options: Disable unnecessary DTD/external-resource resolution and apply explicit resource limits for untrusted input.
Allow all external identifiers by default.
Assume the first successful parse proves the input is safe.
Ignore resource limits when a document is valid XML.
questions.answer_key: Disable unnecessary DTD/external-resource resolution and apply explicit resource limits for untrusted input.
questions.explanation: The correct choice separates the relevant XML concepts and avoids assumptions about processor behavior. Check the linked standard and actual implementation for details.

questions.prompt: After creating an example for “Secure XML Parser Configuration”, what is the best next step?
options: Verify a normal case, an invalid or boundary case, and document the tool/version used.
Rely on visual appearance without parsing or validation.
Change several parts at once and infer the cause if the result changes.
questions.answer_key: Verify a normal case, an invalid or boundary case, and document the tool/version used.
questions.explanation: A small, reproducible test suite distinguishes expected behavior from a lucky example and makes version assumptions visible.
